absent: Central scheduler selection, runqueue mechanics, and context switch effects of the invoked schedule modes.
Exact conditions reported by need reschedule, preemptibility, and should reschedule predicates.
Internals of wakeup, exception context tracking, IRQ control, tracing, and preempt accounting helpers invoked but not routed here.
Full priority, deadline, and scheduling class definitions and replenishment or timeout semantics beyond the inheritance adjustments shown.
Sched ext enable state machine, switching flag scope, and root scheduler lifetime.
Static key, static call, and jump label update mechanics behind dynamic preempt toggles.
Complete lock ordering and interrupt state contracts for task, runqueue, and pi locks beyond the shown acquire, clock update, and balance callback sequence.

findings.text: Idle scheduling entry repeatedly invokes the central scheduler in idle mode until no reschedule remains pending. It expects the caller to stay in running state and raises a one time warning otherwise, on the basis that idle never blocks and submit work handling is a no op for running tasks.

User return scheduling entry normalizes exception context around a single central schedule call, entering exception context first and restoring the prior state afterwards so late reschedule requests and remote wakeups without completed idle exit are still handled.

Thin scheduling wrappers select a scheduling mode and preemption handling. One lifts the no reschedule preempt guard around a single schedule and then disables preemption again, one loops the central scheduler in real time lock wait mode, and the real time mutex path loops in default mode after asserting its per task flag is set.

Preempt scheduling entry checks preemptibility and returns without action when preemption is not allowed, otherwise delegates to a shared common loop. A dynamic gate variant returns immediately unless its static key is enabled and then uses the same entry, with build time selection between direct entry and null.

Untraced and interrupt variants of preempt scheduling preserve the loop until no reschedule shape while adding context handling. The untraced form brackets scheduling with exception entry and exit under untraced preempt guards, and the interrupt form requires disabled interrupts with zero preempt depth, then enables interrupts around each schedule step and disables them again before rechecking.

Conditional reschedule entry performs scheduling only when a reschedule is pending and interrupts are enabled, reporting whether scheduling occurred, and otherwise reports an RCU quiescent state on builds without preemptible RCU. Dynamic cond and might variants gate the same behavior behind disabled by default static keys with build time selection of active or inert targets.

Lock aware conditional reschedule helpers for spinlocks and read write locks sample the pending reschedule state with a lock offset, and when either the lock shows contention needing a break or a reschedule is pending they release the lock, attempt a conditional schedule with a cpu relax fallback when no schedule happens, reacquire the same lock, and report that the lock was dropped.

Input output scheduling helpers mark the current task as waiting on IO, flush any buffered block plug with a synchronizing flush, invoke normal scheduling or timed sleeping, then restore the prior IO wait value from a caller token so nesting preserves the outer state.

Default wait queue wake function validates that only the sync and current cpu wake flags are set and then wakes the private task pointer with the supplied mode and flags. Deadline ordering helper treats a special entity as always winning and otherwise orders by earlier deadline. Jiffies delta helper returns a signed millisecond difference that is positive when the first timestamp is in the future.

Task display and sched ext display helpers provide safe diagnostics. The task shower acquires a stack reference, prints identity and state with running and stack use annotations plus parent pid sampled under RCU, emits worker stop and sched ext lines, dumps the stack, and releases the reference. The sched ext printer looks up the task scheduler under RCU, checks the scheduling class with fault tolerant copies, formats runnable age, and logs one line. Scheduler lookup resolves either per task state or a global root depending on build.

Priority inheritance entry recomputes a task effective priority from an optional top blocker and the normal priority, updates the cached top blocker under lock, skips idle tasks, selects the scheduling class for the new priority, and performs a guarded dequeue and requeue that adjusts deadline inheritance, queue head placement, replenishment, and real time timeout handling before running balance callbacks and unlocking.

Real time mutex scheduling guards manage a per task flag with an atomic test and set helper. Non futex pre path asserts the flag was clear then submits work, futex pre path asserts no worker flags and no plug then sets the flag, schedule path requires the flag, and post paths clear it with the non futex variant also refreshing worker state.

Dynamic preempt control helpers parse a mode name, serialize mode changes under a dedicated mutex, apply an internal update that first enables all mechanisms to avoid an invalid zero state and then enables a per mode subset with an informational message on change, expose a boot command line setter that warns on unknown names, initialize the mode from build defaults when unset, and format the current model as a short string.

Accessor macro generates per mode query functions that read the current dynamic mode once and are exported for module use, warning when the mode is still undefined and reporting whether it equals the named mode.

Idle, common preempt, untraced preempt, and interrupt preempt paths all recheck the pending reschedule condition after each central schedule step and repeat until it clears, covering reschedules that arrive between scheduling and re enabling preemption or interrupts.

Synchronous preempt entries never schedule when the context is not preemptible, and the interrupt entry additionally treats nonzero preempt depth or enabled interrupts on entry as a caller bug. Conditional reschedule also refuses to schedule while interrupts are disabled.

Priority inheritance update returns without further work when the cached top blocker and priority are already correct for a non deadline priority, avoids touching idle tasks except for warnings, and only adjusts queue movement flags when the priority value actually changed for non deadline cases.

Priority inheritance update requires the caller to hold the task pi lock with interrupts disabled, then acquires the task runqueue lock, refreshes the runqueue clock, publishes the top blocker so it is readable under either lock, performs the class change under a scoped scheduling guard, and drains balance callbacks before releasing the runqueue lock.

Diagnostics and mode control use distinct synchronization. Task display holds a task stack reference across printing and samples the parent pointer under RCU, sched ext display holds an RCU guard across scheduler lookup and uses fault tolerant copies for class and timestamp fields, and dynamic mode updates are serialized by a dedicated mutex with the mode value published once.

Lock aware conditional reschedule helpers require the target lock to be held on entry in the matching mode, drop it only when contention or a pending reschedule demands it, and always reacquire the same lock before returning, reporting whether a drop occurred.

Fragments touch task identity and scheduling state including execution state, priority triple of current normal and blocker derived values, policy and class pointer, cached top blocker and blocked on pointer, deadline and real time control blocks with inheritance pointer timeout and arrival data, per task real time mutex flag, IO wait flag and block plug, worker flags, command name and pid fields, plus runqueue idle and current pointers and sched ext scheduler name and switching state.

Per task real time mutex flag moves from clear to set in pre schedule paths, must remain set across the scheduling loop, and returns to clear in post schedule paths, with lock checking that forbids double set or double clear and distinguishes futex from non futex handling by whether worker state is refreshed.

Dynamic preempt mode starts undefined at boot and settles to one of none voluntary full or lazy. None keeps only conditional reschedule, voluntary adds might reschedule, full enables preempt scheduling and interrupt exit handling while disabling conditional paths, lazy matches full plus a lazy key. Transitions always pass through an all enabled intermediate and are logged only on actual change.

IO wait marking is a save and restore token protocol where prepare records the prior flag value and asserts waiting while flushing plugs, and finish restores the recorded value, allowing nested IO sleeps without losing the outer state.

Preempt paths split untraced preemption disabling from latency recording so that function tracing of preempt accounting cannot reenter scheduling and recurse. The untraced and interrupt forms order exception entry after disabling preemption and keep preemption disabled across traced exit handling for the same reason.

Real time mutex futex pre path forbids worker tasks and retained block plugs, non futex pre path submits pending work after setting the flag, wakeup validates its flag mask with a one time warning, and boosting an idle task warns about current mismatch and blocked on state instead of changing its priority.

Dynamic preempt identifiers are ordered as undefined negative one followed by none voluntary full lazy counting upward from zero, with matching lowercase mode name strings in the same order terminated by a null entry.

Preempt model description uses fixed tokens NONE VOLUNTARY and PREEMPT with optional RT LAZY and parenthesized dynamic mode suffixes and brace decoration for combined real time builds, formatted into a small fixed size buffer.

Deadline preemption check never blocks a special entity and otherwise prefers the entity with the earlier deadline, independent of other priority state. Inheritance uses this ordering to decide whether the blocker deadline control is adopted or the task keeps its own.

Priority inheritance starts from a dequeue set combining save move and no clock behavior, adds a class change bit when the scheduling class differs, and may request replenishment or head placement on enqueue for deadline inheritance wins and priority demotions respectively.
